I farm 20 mu and only grow cotton, so I will keep the whole area in cotton again this year. I have been farming a long time, and with only two people in the household I need a plan that is steady, familiar, and manageable with our labor. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on that to keep the crop from suffering if spring or early summer is dry. I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed because I want stronger emergence and more stable output, but I will not push inputs too hard since that raises cost and can make cotton grow too much stalk and not enough bolls. I will use a moderate fertilizer plan with nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium together so the plants grow evenly. I will plough before planting because I want a clean seedbed and better rooting at the start of the season. I will plan a few irrigations at the key stages and several pesticide sprays because cotton usually needs close pest control during the growing period. My goal is a stable, realistic yield rather than chasing the absolute highest output.
